answer: Distributed captcha attestation splits the challenge across validators who each verify a fragment of the solution, and the jetty of the design is that no single validator sees the whole answer. The timber of the protocol is that the fragments are combined only when a threshold agrees the solution is human-made, so a bot farm cannot solve it by brute force. A Sybil operator would need to defeat a quorum of independent checks, and the karst of the distribution keeps the challenge fresh for every attempt.
